memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "The LORD was with Joseph so that he prospered, and he lived in the house of his Egyptian master. When his master saw that the LORD was with him and that the LORD gave him success in everything he did, Joseph found favor in his eyes and became his attendant. Potiphar put him in charge of his household, and he entrusted to his care everything he owned" - Gen 39:2-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the key that unlocks the whole chapter: "The LORD was with Joseph." Notice where this is said — not in a palace, but in slavery. Joseph is a slave in a foreign house, and yet the Lord is with him, and it shows. He is faithful, diligent, and trustworthy, and Potiphar soon puts him in charge of the entire household.

We must be careful how we read the word "prospered." Joseph was still a slave; God's presence did not lift him out of his hard situation. What it did was bless his work and his character right in the middle of it. God's presence does not always change our circumstances, but it always changes us, and it makes our faithfulness fruitful even in hard places.

Notice too that Joseph did not sulk or slack off because life was unfair. He served with excellence, even as a slave, and God blessed it. He worked "as for the Lord" long before Paul ever wrote those words (Col 3:23). His integrity was visible enough that even a pagan master could see God's hand on him.

If you are in a hard or unfair situation, the message of Joseph is not "God will quickly rescue you," but something better: "God is with you." Serve faithfully where you are, and let His presence make you a person others can see He is with.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do you serve faithfully even in hard or unfair situations?
Is God's presence in your life visible to those around you?
How does "the LORD was with him" change how you face your circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You are with me even in hard places. Help me to serve faithfully wherever I am, working as unto You, so that others may see Your hand upon my life. Amen.
